Terrible experience, will never go back due to the way we were treated! I have never had this experience at a restaurant even in Chicago where we are from. My sister lives in Philadelphia and she was appalled at the way the owner Robin Barg treated us. 
We were told there was a 30 minute wait. My husband and I were waiting for the table while my sister was still on her way. The table was ready in 10 minutes so we sat down knowing she was going to arrive shortly. 
Robin came to the table 3 minutes later asking where our 3rd person is and next time we should not take the table if we are not all there, because she could have sat someone else. We said she will be here in a few minutes, then she proceeded to tell us that we can write a bad yelp review if we want, but that we should not have taken the table because it throws everything off and the waiter has to keep checking on us.
Then five minutes later again she came back and said "ok guys, what's going on?" My husband and I had ordered juice and coffee and assured her that she will arrive any minute. I asked her what the difference is if we needed extra time looking at the menu or decided to stay longer after our meal to converse. Would we be forced to leave? Meanwhile a table of 6 left and the few people that were waiting were able to get seated. She made us feel so uncomfortable and we couldn't possibly stay to eat and have a good experience after that. Just as we decided to leave because we couldn't believe the way she was treating us, my sister walked in! 
So after only 7-10 minutes, we were harassed twice! Another couple heard what happened and walked out with us and said they would never return. 
My sister will never go back or recommend it. Even from a previous experience she had saying that the food was just ok and the portions were extremely small.

I liked the food alright. But the portions were, dare I say, TOO BIG!? I mean you could feed a family of three with one of these meals. In fact I would suggest order sparingly to anyone going here. I mean, a lot of food for very little money, isn't a huge problem, but it just feels wrong to be served this much food. Am I the only one who feels this way?

I was greeted by a really friendly worker when I walked into this shop. It was like a half basement kind of thing. However, there was plenty of seating to be found and the food came out pretty quick!

I got the Luke's trio in order to try out all of them. By far, the shrimp and the lobster rolls were the best. They really give you a lot of the meat! However, even though the rolls were "half" rolls, they were as small as my fist (Donald trump size). Sad to say the taste is excellent (except maybe for crab, a little under-seasoned I felt) with perfectly toasted rolls with butter (crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside), the price to quantity ratio was not it. It was 21 dollars overall, and I'd probably spend 18 dollars next time to get two full shrimp rolls.

They have a lot of unique bottled drinks though, if you are into trying out new things. 

Overall, tasty food, but the portion sizes are too small for my liking. (If you eat little, it will be worth for you!)

Mike's Hot Dog Cart should really be called Mike's Hot Sausage Truck because he stands at the back of his truck making the best hot sausage sandwich in Philly. So what you say? Try one. both.review_text:
Not 3.5 but not quite 4 stars and Only been once so bear with me, the staff was extremely friendly and nice which is always great and the food is very Authentic and delicious. The menu is HUGE! And extensive with a variety to fit anyone's palette, even had an American style section for those less adventurous patrons( I steered clear of that section and would advise others to do so as well, kinda ruins the point of going to an authentic spot ya know?) 

For starters I got the Dan Dan noodles and had them make it as spicy as possible,even told them don't hold back, not like " American" spicy and she chuckled. They were alright not that flavorful( in comparison to Han) and really not fiery how I was hoping,very little heat to me but I'm am a chili head by true nature so go figure. I also got the wontons in chili oil ordered as is no adjusting heat and they were Delish!! I wish I had ordered them spicier because it wasn't at all but my friend who doesn't take heat well thought they were spicy enough, so an individual take on heat level. 

My friend and I didn't even order our entrees off of the menu as we were peeking on the table next to ours and saw a few great options. She got braised pork belly which we later found had tofu in it and we aren't tofu people but the tofu was a firmer one and flavorful so okay and the pork belly was super tender with melty fat perfect for those who like different textures. Has an herb that gave a odd aftertaste but still fine. I got the crispy dry pepper shrimp ordered super hot and it was great! The shrimp was super crispy and even still crispy after a day in the fridge for left overs , was impressed. The heat was not where I wanted it but the shrimp size and portion made up for it.  The meal was really affordable as well. 

Coming back to browse the menu some without a doubt

This place is way overpriced and definitely lacking in their portions sizes for the prices of their entrees. The step down dining, is something I like. It's a slightly dark place. The lighting from the small track lights above do just enough illumination. It reminds me of a reformed wine cellar. The booths are tall, yet you sit at ground level. All around you are those scientific artist renderings of various species of seafood. Be that as it may, I wasn't impressed. Where as with Lacroix, I was treated to something special. This was kind of normal, average. I digress. I really love their complementary biscuit, served with sweet butter cream. More please! For our appetizer we had the small order of Muscles in garlic butter juice. I love seafood and Muscles especially. There was enough for the both of us and it came with a nice size of (Sourdough?) garlic bread. I ordered a glass of Cline Los Carneros Syrah. For my entree I had the Fried Shrimp. This was your standard 10, large, butterflied Shrimp. With fries and Cole Slaw. Again, nothing special. It tasted as it should. There was no special way the Shrimp was fried other than Panko bread crumbs. Then again, I use Panko bread crumbs when I make the frozen Mac-n-Cheese from Trader Joe's. Nothing special there you see???? My lady had The "Jumbo" Lump Crab Cakes with Asparagus and Mashed Potatoes. Her crab cakes were seasoned and spiced with special ingredients garnish etc. The mash was done up too. Really becasue she had a greater variety of a meal, her entree was the more enticing. But, there was no JUMBO in her 2 measly crab cakes. They were two 4oz scoops, if that's what JUMBO means. Her mash was like 2 table spoons smeared into a ball. She had some Riesling with her dinner as well. She agreed after we left that for close to $95 the food was good, not spectacular. The portion sizes were very underwhelming (yes, I understand that good restaurants will portion control to preserve the integrity of the food. It is dining at a higher level so there is more to consider. It's also about keeping cost down etc.). We just feel we didn't get our money's worth.
Just okay. The food quality was good but incredibly overpriced. And I mean incredibly!

keyword_only.review_text: Khyber Pass Pub is like a little secret spot tucked away in the Old City area.  Really affordable, perfectly flavored, and perfectly cooked BBQ and sides.  Exceptional (without being too pushy) service.  Note: I don't really eat meat, so I just got the macaroni and cheese side.  However, the side was out of this world delicious.  They also had some vegan options that sounded so good, I kind of didn't understand them.  Vegan pulled pork?  What would that be like?  So needless to say, I was too scared to try them.  But after seeing everyone else's dishes, I now know I should have just bit the bullet and given them a try!

Way too pretentious and over priced for the food they serve. 

Surf and turf was almost bad. 

The ice cream taco desert was very good but no idea why they are serving such an unsophisticated dish in a place that wants to be Le Bec Fin. 

One other thing, the backwaiter yelled 'excuse me' every time he came to bring something to or clear the table. I don't get it?

This was the best breakfast sandwich I've ever had. The whole thing was perfect. Additionally the hash brown was out of this world. It's also reasonably priced! Highly recommend making this a stop on any visit to Philly!

semantic_only.review_text: My reviews don't usually start with comments on service because honestly the food is the only thing that truly matters at a restaurant to me. That said, the service a Zahav was impeccable! Our waiter was knowledgeable, kind, engaging, friendly, etc. Now on to the food. It's mostly tapas which is a great way to try lots of things without breaking the bank. The great:The hummus with bread straight from the oven, the duck hearts(my favorite), ground duck and foie gras, crispy grape leaves, kibble naya, coffee custard with marshmallow. the average:cauliflower, grilled haloumi, eggplant, pistachio tart. The Disappointing:roasted turnips.(can't win them all). On a Monday at 8pm the place was rocking! Lively atmosphere with a higher than normal noise level and lots happy diners. I had reservations but overheard there was 1 hour wait for the bar and that tables were fully booked. Price point was actually a bit lower than what I expected for a restaurant of this caliber(rare thing).

OVERRATED!! It was expensive and not even that good. Dinner for two of us was $200 and we ordered one drink each and no dessert. Speaking of dessert, the options were meh. We ended up going somewhere else to get dessert that night. We ordered about 5 plates and ended up really liking only one of them. It absolutely wasn't worth the high price tag. Save your money and go somewhere else.

Every detail shines through here, from the classically and beautifully styled rooms, tables and bars to a simple brunch meal. The beer list is well curated and the fact you can get a 20oz pour of your top choice ( I went with the Prima Pils) adds a little extra joy. 

A great place for dinner with the parents or to celebrate a special occasion, or even just because sometimes you want a big beer and a classic English breakfast. 

I chose a sausage egg and cheese with triple fried chips. Not health food by any means but so good you'll happily loosen your belt. The bread is buttery and a little crispy, with great flavor in the meat and satisfying texture from the gooey cheese and an egg that runs ever so slightly. The fries were thick, but crispy and we'll seasoned. Dessert and coffee satisfied, though I can't say it excelled. 

Staff and service are strong, cool without being aloof. Price is reasonable given the strength of the meal and the impressive aesthetics - a visual treat.

semantic_only_weak_tail.review_text: Following the news of late? They need to fumigate this jawn. Mice, roaches and feces.

Thank you Charlotte for helping me over the phone! I super appreciated you accommodating my needs last minute. That was so very  kind of you to help and your team as well even when it caused more work!
Girl at the desk terrible person she made me wait for looong time! Didn't even say any info...

both.review_text: After Very long wait time (even with a reservation) the server took approximately 30 min to come take our appetizer order. I believe we had the one and only wobbly unstable table at the restaurant (by the street). Our entrees were cold upon serving. With all of this being, the staff was friendly and apologetic.

Our experience started less than desirably.  We arrived on time for an 8:30 reservation.  Unfortunately, friends of ours were unable to get a babysitter so we contacted the restaurant earlier in the day and they said it would be no problem. When we arrived the hostess acted as if they had no clue.  My husband got us drinks at the bar, but that took more than 15 minutes.  We continued to wait for our table, so my husband inquired with the host. We were then seated 20 minutes late.  Be ware, there is no place to wait, so the entire time you are waiting for your table you are bumped by waiters, waitress, and other patrons.  Perhaps there should be a limit on the number of people permitted in the upstairs bar area.  We ordered the chef's tasting menu.  Our entire service was completed in an hour, 10 courses in 1 hour.  I have never in my life had food brought to me to quickly.  I felt extremely rushed.  There was a couple seated next to us who complained to the manager prior to getting seated, due to their long wait.  At least they were comped for their bad experience. Now to the food, it was average.  Nothing spectacular, nothing inedible.  Just average.  Our dinner concluded with dessert and our waitress didn't even ask if we wanted coffee; as I noticed other tables around us getting this.  All in all, I was disappointed with the experience, the initial wait and the service. As I stated the food was average.  I have attended happy hour in the upstairs space on a prior occasion and felt the experience was much better.

I was pretty disappointed with the experience I had at this restaurant, possibly because I had high expectations from previous reviews. There wasn't a wait to be seated but there was an extremely long wait to be served! So long that we required refills on our drinks before receiving our meals... and that was another wait to even be noticed that a refill was needed. When the food arrived after about 45 minutes or more! My plate wasn't even full! It was a very skimpy meal!

The table next to us had 3 older ladies who also had the same wait as us in addition to one of the ladies not being able to eat her meal because it was too spicy. Another dish had to be boxed for her because once she received it, her friends had already finished eating.

The food itself was ok, nothing worth coming out my way for again

keyword_only.review_text:
Did I really pay $20 for a burger? Yup. Was it the best. burger. ever.? Yup. 

I was feeling a little under the weather when I went to Village Whiskey and really was looking forward to a nice hot toddy more than anything, which didn't disappoint. I wasn't even sure about ordering food since I didn't know how well I could taste, but the hostess offered us a seat at the "back table" which turned out to be fine and we ordered burgers and fries. 

"Burgers and fries" is a total understatement. We got two orders of fries-- one with cheese and one plain. Both were delicious but the real deal here is the burgers. I ordered mine with carmelized onion and bacon. My friend got cheddar cheese and bacon. I have no idea what they do to these burgers but they are seriously gourmet. Even the rolls are rich. 

Our server was nice and helpful with questions about the menu, but service was really slow. The restaurant was definitely packed, but even ordering beers took a long time and our second order of fries took forever. 

One last note about the crowd-- definitely not what I expected. Mostly over 40 but very fun-- we were sitting in an area that was crowded with people standing and people were chatty. In retrospect and in reading other reviews, we were lucky to be seated right away. Seating is extremely limited and very cramped, even at the actual tables. Next time we will try going on a weeknight.

Great service, Great atmosphere & great food. We had a reservation & we were seated right away which doesn't happen at many restaurants. Our server, Lisa, really knew the menu & helped us make great selections. She definitely made the whole experience! The food was delicious too.  
I had the Tempura Shrimp & Vegetables and loved it.  We will go back!

I brought a party of 6 here for dinner last weekend and we loved our experience! We arrived early on a Friday (about 5:30) and were seated immediately. I was surprised at the decor. It was not exactly latin inspired, I just remember it being very dark. They had multiple TVs which my boyfriend and his friends enjoyed to watch basketball on. We ordered a few pitchers of their house margaritas which were amazing. They are not your typical Mexican joint's neon green "margaritas". These were fresh squeezed, strong, and had a hint of pineapple juice to them. So good! The waiter was very attentive in refilling our glasses for us which we liked. I had the Tuna tacos and my boyfriend had skirt steak. Both were excellent! We thought the tuna was the better of the two. My only regret is that we did not order the tuna guacamole as well. Our bill was pricy but that was to be expected. We did not mind paying it after getting such great service, delicious food and tasty drinks. I definitely want to come back to Sancho Pistolas for happy hour next!

semantic_only.review_text:
I just want to say, we could not even step into your restaurant because you, for some reason, keep skipping us and not even trying setting us up with the table when we know we got there way before some people that you have already found the table for your other customers. So when we got there, girl with the tablet told us it would be 30 to 40 minutes until the table is available. We walked around and came back. When we came back, man who had a cell phone said 10 to 15 minutes. Then we waited at near the door. Still waited while people who were there after us got to sit. 

We asked if our table is ready, he said another 10 to 15 minutes. We just left. And after another 1 hour and 30 minutes later, we received the text stating our table is ready. 

Total waiting time: 2 hours and 30 minutes.

I dont care how your food is good. You literally didn't let us sit for some reason. Glad you have customers. But no thanks.

One of the best places in Philly.  I've been here a few times over the last couple years (great date spot). The ambience is great,  not too dark but relaxed.  The food is spectacular.  The kitchen is open (you can sit at a bar along the kitchen) so you know everything is fresh. While there my favorite things were the meatballs which had a seasoning akin to what you would use in italian sausage and the ricotta which I could have eaten by the bucketfull. I also had the pappardelle in a meat sauce which wasn't bad, but wasn't great (the pasta was too thick and the meat sauce was bland).  Whats great about the food is they are mostly small plates so you can drive a bunch of different things.  Their cocktail menu is solid with a good variety (i had an old fashioned that wasn't bad), but you come here for the food.  The service was excellent and the wait is long for a table (30-60 mins) if you don't have a reservation.

both.review_text: We were very pleased to get a lovely booth when we arrived. Our server was excellent and the food terrific. The restaurant is very attractive and inviting. However, the restaurant is SO NOISY that we had difficulty conversing and enjoying our meal. There was loud rock like music on the sound system which does not go with such a fine restaurant. In addition there were large groups nearby that added to the noise. It is unfortunate and we would never return. The Prices are VERY high. It is just not worth it.

We tried to have brunch here while in town to visit some museums.  As we entered the restaurant, we noticed that while not completely pack, it was very loud and noisy.  When we were seated, we could not even hold a conversation unless we were speaking very loud.  We ended up leaving and not ordering anything.  We actually grabbing a bite and eating in the park, less noise if you want to ha e a conversation.

This place was fine when my friend and I were the only ones in the restaurant; then when the place began to fill up it became so loud that it was truly unbearable.  It was so noisy that we had to shout at each other from across our two-top and eventually stopped our conversation altogether. Mediocre food, mediocre service, unacceptably loud.  Will not be returning.

keyword_only.review_text: Still a solid place for brunch in West. It's quiet, friendly, byo and serves a nice variety for brunch. I got the chicken and waffles and the chicken was juicy and tender and the waffles were fluffy and buttery. I like the ease of this place. It has a very nice vibe. However, just a personal opinion, but the atmosphere would be on a sweeter level if there were nice music playing (one night, long ago, when dining here, I remember such a lovely jazz play list that floated through the dining room)  that filled the restaurant with sweet sounds instead of the large, looming TV that was playing sports. This seems like an odd choice to me as a place that has such somewhat elevated choices on their menu shouldn't be giving out "sports bar vibes". However, if you are ok with that,  it's still a nice place for a tasty brunch.

I live two blocks away and consider myself pretty lucky to have a place like this within a short walk. There's definitely a hipster vibe and sometimes I feel out of place, but everyone is cool and easy to talk to.

Food is just flat out solid. I've never had something I didn't enjoy, and every dish is unique in its own way. The beer rotation and the fun atmosphere is what puts it over the edge and compels me to give them 5 stars. One of the most enjoyable restaurants I have ever been patronized.

This is definitely a sushi favorite.
Their special rolls are amazing! It's made well and when it comes to your table, it looks great and tastes like it! I don't know who their sushi chef is but he creates miracles!
It opens for lunch and then closes to reopen for dinner. And although, street parking is a bit difficult to find, this place is probably my number one in the city for sushi. The ambience is very modern and it can be a little quiet at times even though there is conversation going on. Great for couples and small groups.
Recommended this place to friends and they all said they loved it. It's worth to try this place at least once.

semantic_only.review_text:
A hard review to write, as i loved the food and thought that our server was fantastic. But, this was without any doubt, the single loudest restaurant that I've ever been to. It was loud enough to significantly effect my experience. 

If you are in anyway sensitive to noise or, if like me, just simply prefer a quieter atmosphere, this is by no means an option.

I've been here before. Food and margs are decent, but the noise level was UNCOMFORTABLY LOUD! I HAD TO MOVE MY CHAIR TO THE SIDE IN THE HOPES I COUKD HEAR MY DINNER COMPANION. IT DIDN'T WORK! When I asked the waiter if it was always this loud on a Friday night, he shrugged and replied, "If people are talking loudly." A trip through the restaurant to the bathroom confirmed it was loud everywhere. SO APPARENTLY PEOPLE TALK LOUD AT THE BAR, IN A DINING ROOM.... If you go, go on a warm evening and sit on the patio if you would like to have a conversation that isn't punctuated by "Huh?" and "What?".

The food is awesome, but it is so incredibly loud there it's not a very pleasant place to eat. I came for a date with my boo, and we had to scream at each other above the din. It was hard to relax and enjoy the food, because it was impossible to have a conversation. It is pretty crowded (easy to bang elbows with your neighbor) and that doesn't help the noise sitch since you can hear them screaming as well. Maybe if I was at the bar for a lively drink it would be fun, but the care put into the food is not matched by care put into the experience of eating the food.

semantic_only_weak_tail.review_text:
This place has the BEST Italian bread in the City...
They also make the BEST EASTER BREAD you can buy! Been eating their breads for 46 years!

I make hubby stop here on his lunch break once a week and buy several loaves for me at once. I have a freezer in my basement so I cut it up, ziploc it and pop it in oven to warm up again when needed. It's delicious even after freezing/thawing. My kids are addicted to their breads! I dip them in garlic olive oil. So yummy!

This local bakery is a few blocks from my apartment and is one of the best Bakeries in town. Delicious bread and incredibly low priced. It's a tiny little shop on the corner and they have weird hours. If you are in the area when they are open, I would highly recommended stopping by! 

They only have a few different selections of breads but all are freshly baked. Definitely worth the trip.

both.review_text: My family and I absolutely love this place.  The food is amazing and the service is wonderful.  We've been two times and both times everything was perfect.  The mushroom appetizer is to die for! The veal is so tender and delicious that you can cut it with a fork.  We have gotten the veal viola, veal carciofi, linguine pizzaioli (which has veal, capers and olives in a spicy red sauce), and the chicken rollatini.  The prices are reasonable and the portions are huge.  The veal/chicken dishes are served with vegetables, so a side of spaghetti costs extra, but it's so worth it! The side is huge and the red sauce is hands-down the freshest, most delicious sauce I've had since being in Italy.  The restaurant is BYOB and the outdoor area is picturesque with all of the overhead lights.  The desserts are reasonably priced and delicious, we especially loved the tiramisu and the cannoli cake.  Lastly, the staff is friendly, welcoming and attentive.

I am here often as I travel to Philly alot. There food is hit or miss. Some items on the menu are great (their burgers and breakfast sausage) and some are bland (their cheesesteak and cheesesteak omelet, which is kind of sad since it IS a PHIL airport restaurant). 

Although sometimes I have a good experience with the food, and sometimes there is room for improvement, I can say that they should look more into their staff. 

I have rarely had good service here, and I am hear a LOT. You order via ipad screen, which is convenient (I really like that) but to me, that is also another reason the service should be better, because its less work for them. They don't even have to take your order. 

I sat here the other day (close to the bar) and heard 3-4 20ish  year old waitresses complaining, and talking about the customers, and gossiping about the other staff. It was the ENTIRE time I was there (at least an hour, they didnt stop). They all had a story about one of their customers that irritated them, and the customers were there at that moment. Immature and rude staff. 

I would suggest some training and management oversight here.

This place is pretty awesome. Xfinity Live made a great move by getting rid of the fancy shmancy restaurant that used to be there and putting this one in. It has more of a polished and professional vibe than the other 3 places at Xfinity, but still has a young, fun atmosphere.

The food was great. It's a nice change of pace to see unique menu offerings at a place full of sports bars if you're not in the mood for wings or a burger. They also have a nice selection of vegetarian options for people like my room mate who normally only has 1-2 options on the menu when we go out to eat. Do yourself a favor and get the cheese fundido with house-made chips!

I'm normally a beer drinker but I tried one of their signature cocktails (and tried sips of my friend's drinks) and they were all amazing. I'd go back just for one of those drinks!!

Last but not least, service was perfect. Staff was friendly, knowledgable, and attentive without being overbearing. Our waitress gave great recommendations and asked for feedback. All in all, it was a great experience!

keyword_only.review_text: We live multiple hours away, but we come to philly often. We love coming here when we're in the mood for Mexican. Consistently delicious. Our last server was awesome, coming from two service-industry people. He was smart, quick, attentive, but gave us some space, all while training a new server.  I can't come here without ordering the queso fundido, and I'm lactose intolerant. I haven't had everything yet, but the items I've ordered in between trips have always been consistent. I have no plans of finding anywhere else to enjoy tequila and Mexican food while in philly.

I love this bar, and will go out of my way to end the night here. Prices are good, their food is AMAZING, a huge selection of beer on tap, and great service. Tons of TVs and lively atmosphere during sporting events. You might consider getting there early, though, as it gets pretty busy, but for good reason, and it's totally worth it.

I brought my family here recently because I had been interested in trying it for a while. I loved that you could get a free "Mix Meze" appetizer just by checking in on Yelp. We enjoyed all six of the items and the waitress kindly brought us as much pita as we asked for. We also ordered the Manti (Turkish ravioli) which I have never had before, it was amazing and probably my favorite dish in the entire meal. The raviolis were great and the yogurt sauce was also amazing. Amongst my family, we ordered the Prime Time Steak, Pan Seared Seabass (or possibly the catch of the day, can't remember), the Kasap Kofte (ground beef patties), Lamb Chops. We all tried bits of everything, the fish dish was amazing. I thought the steak was slightly dry though, and the kasap kofte and lamb chops slightly over done. I wish one of us had ordered a chicken dish. I would come back to try that or the Kushbashi! (filet mignon). For dessert we ordered a baklava and Kunefe. I absolutely LOVED the baklava, it wasn't too sweet but sweet enough. (And I'm pretty picky about the baklava). The kunefe was a little interesting, I have too much of a sweet tooth to have enjoyed that (we described it to each other like shredded wheat and a sweetened mozzarella type cheese). Our waitress was very sweet and attentive. However, the dishes did take a very long time to come out and the main courses also came out at different times which can be difficult with a group of people. I would come back again though!

semantic_only.review_text: Food is amazing. Staff are so rude, impatient, and unfriendly. They rolled their eyes at us multiple times, snatched the menus out of our hands, and were incredibly curt

There are just a few airport bars I really like, and this is (close to being) one of them.

Jet Rock has many positives - chief among them being the draft beer selection: 48 quality pulls, skewing heavily towards the ales.  Whiskey (or whisky, depending upon your potable preference) lovers will appreciate choosing from among 19 single malts and blends.

Don't like draft?  Fear not, they have two bottled beers as well, 

The bar itself, a grand sweeping behemoth studded with fluorescing ceramic and brass draft-towers, is the central eyepiece in this concourse.  The wall is lined with a few high-tops, and a mawing cavern awaits those to be seated at a traditional 4-top.  This area, while truly an image of purgatory for any agoraphobics out there, at least offers a view of the tarmac.  wow.

Their food is, in general, not bad, but please stay away from the Philly Cheese Steak sammich with Cheese Wiz.  I warned you.

Other than that, I have ordered several satisfying dishes, but my favorite so far has simply been their burgers, which are excellent!  They also have decent salads, which you might want to get instead of the fries, which are waayyy too salty.  Horrible.  They exist only to coerce you into drinking more beer.  Come on, peeps!  You do not have to do much to get me to drink more beer.  Simply having beer to sell is sufficient.

Now, I am a huge Guinness fan, but their Guinness here is occasionally off-tasting.  The last time I was here it was not drinkable.  The strange thing about that is that the staff knew it was bad, and served it to me anyway, without warning, and apparently in some vain attempt to get me to take the shite off their hands.

This brings me squarely to the staff - by far the biggest weakness in the establishment.

Generally I am very staff friendly, but this place simply has consistently bad staff, with a pervasive poor attitude, low attentiveness, and a nonchalant incivility.  This is exacerbated during any rush when they just seem to be put out.  ("Customers are really very annoying, aren't they?  Always wanting us to do shit for them!"

Too bad.  Would have gotten a four.

As a college student, I love Banana Leaf. It can be rowdy at times but it's always a good time. We tend to go in a group with a few boxes of wine (BYOB). It's not uncommon for the restaurant to be loud with college kids, which can be good or bad. Our group doesn't mind as we are also loud college kids.

The menu is pretty large and there will be something for everyone in your party. Start with the Roti Canai. It's delicious, the "bread" itself has a good texture and the sauce they serve it with compliments it very well. When I went yesterday, I had the Captain's Noodles with flat noodles. It was pretty good. I've also had their spicy chicken, curry chicken, and pad Thai. There are a ton more things on the menu that I would like to try. Also, the fried ice cream is good. Everything on the menu is extremely affordable. The staff can seem "pushy" at times but I think there just trying to provide the best service they can. They are also helpful with menu recommendations.

both.review_text:
We found the food to be too spicy to be able to taste the other flavors.  Everyone in my group arrived thinking we enjoyed spicy food.  Apparently we do not.  We ordered only dishes that had mid-level heat ratings (4-6) and found that with only one exception the flavors were overpowered by the chilies.  
The \dish we most enjoyed were the dan dan noodles.
So,if everyone in your group likes really, really hot food this is the place for you.

I've been to this place a couple of times with a group of people and in general thought it was good. I definitely enjoy going back, however I've had mixed experiences with the spice level. The menu is helpful because it indicates the spice level of each meal, although the lowest is three, I think. Definitely could make more dishes that appeal to those of us that don't like spicy. The first time I went I got a meal that was advertised as three (to them not spicy) and asked for no peppers and mild. It came out perfect and I loved it. However the next time the waitress seemed annoyed and it came out spicier. That is my only complaint, so for those who need mild dishes, just be adamant and careful about it. However, overall great food and I will definitely be going back!

It was late at night and since so much of Philly seems to shutdown early, we didn't know where to eat.  On the advice from our hotel's concierge we hit up Continental Midtown.  When we walked in I didn't get the best feeling.  The place looks like you are walking onto the set of the Brady Bunch and a bad 70s disco all at once.  The set up is strange, the levels feel like the inside of a old department store with the glass siding and wood trim on the top.  Whoever designed the look of this place is trying way too hard to  be different...and failing.  

It was around 11 and the only seating left was on the second floor.  That was fine, but where I had to sit was not.  They have 70s looking wicker seats that are suspended from the ceiling.  Maybe to some people this seems hip.  To me however, the novelty of it never even starts let alone wear off.  The seats are very uncomfortable and by the time we left my back and legs was in pain.  It's just not a seat meant for dining, it's way too awkward.  

The music began OK even though it was extremely loud.  After the first two songs, the music just went completely downhill.  There was no consistency.  The songs went from current indie songs, to 80s "new wave" to just loud bass thumping poor club music.  Very odd.  Decor and music, two strike outs.

The server was friendly.  She tells us they are out of szechuan shoestring fries.  That sucked since we were going to order that.  We tell her we need more time.  She comes back and just as we are about to order the BBQ chicken entree, she tells us they just ran out of that as well.  It was a Friday night, how are they running out of food?  Very amateurish.

We finally get the food we ordered, the food they didn't run out of.  One of the entrees is very spicy.  There was zero indication on the menu that the food would be spicy.  I thought that was weird.  We tell the server and she quickly offers to give us a new replacement entree that is less spicy.  She tells us they have a spicy and a not spicy version.  Why didn't she tell us that before we ordered it?
 
The server and the food were good, but the rest killed any enjoyment I would have gotten out of the place.  I would not recommend it and I would never return.

keyword_only.review_text: I frequent AmeriThai a lot during lunch time and also order take out and delivery.  Service is always excellent.  The owner is always smiling and always friendly and she remembers my name every time. Everything that I've tried was delicious.  I've had the pad thai, crazy noodles, nhem khao, papaya salad, Tom yum soup and the pho.  The only thing is some of the dishes are spicy and it doesn't state it in the menu.  So when ordering, make sure to ask if it is spicy or not and tell them how you handle your spice.  The nhem khao and papaya salad were both way too spicy for me when I first ordered them.  But when I told them my preference of spice it was good.  Definitely worth a try!

Passed by here a few times. Finally got a chance to try it. We got there at 12:30 and there was only two other people. I ordered the spicy ramen- the ramen was good. Nice and chewy. But the broth was thick. I am used to thin broth. Not too spicy either. Overall, I won't be back because there are other good ramen places in Chinatown.

I'm sitting here eating breakfast. The orange juice tastes fresh squeezed - delicious! I ordered the eggs benedict with much hesitation. They are made with a sriaccha hollandaise and placed on Belgium waffles. I was fearful they would be too spicy. I can't stress enough how perfect they tasted! The breakfast potatoes were equally as delicious! I highly recommend this breakfast! The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because there were crumbs on the seat and the hostess wasn't friendly.

semantic_only.review_text:
If you are wondering around Reading Market Terminal and absolutely overwhelmed, look for Carmen's because it has the longest line of all time. I went on a Sunday morning and I thought it would be quiet. To my surprise, it was the complete opposite!! The line wrapped around the corner and it was only getting longer as I waited.

Man oh man did I make the choice to commit the line! Watching the cooks make the philly cheesesteaks and hoagies make the whole experience mouthwatering. 
You must eat this while its hot!!! Don't let this baby get cold!!

The food ordered:

The Classic Cheesesteak: (5/5)
Sweet roasted pepper, cheese wiz
I have never been so happy before with a philly cheesesteak. The amount of meat was proportionate to the bread. 

Kamikaze Cheesesteak: (4/5)
All the peppers and hot sauce complimented the whole cheese steak. I'm a huge fan of spicy so in all honesty, it wasn't really that spicy. The menu makes it sound spicy.

Came here recently with a group of friends - the ambiance is nice, and we were seated promptly with our reservation. The bay windows out front were wide open and fresh cool air was coming in - looked like were were in for a great night.

Although I got to try a couple of the things that other people ordered, I'm just going to focus on the two dishes that I ordered:

1. Dan Dan Noodles - 3/5. I was a little disappointed with this - not really a whole lot of heat/numbing sensation with this one. And the noodles weren't as chewy as I had hoped for. I'd definitely say that Han's Dynasty still has a huge advantage over them here. 

2. Silken tofu with fish in hot chili oil - 4/5. I really was looking forward to this dish because I was hoping to get a good combination of numbing spice and strong heat. This dish is rated "3/3" on their menu and supposedly is one of the spiciest dishes they offer. It came out in a relatively small pot and after several pieces of fish and servings of sauce over rice, my tongue was sufficiently numb and tingling. However, I didn't feel the heat that it was supposed to bring. After our meal was over, our waitress asked us how everything was. I expressed my surprise that my dish was not as spicy as I had thought it would be, and she proceeded to tell me that she had lowered the spiciness of my order from a 3 to 2. Excuse me? Why would you do such a thing. I came here to THIS restaurant because I like SPICY food. My only complaint of this dish was it wasn't spicy enough and you're telling me now that you had it prepared less spicy without my request? 

Although I kept this internal for our dinner, I fumed a little inside. I got over it (well, I think so) and I'd be willing to try it again - and although I don't think one should have to request the spiciness that is listed on the menu, I will be sure to make sure that I receive what I order.

I'd come back - not for the Dan Dan Noodles - but for trying out some of their other Szechuan dishes.

Once you've tasted hand-drawn noodles, you'll never want any other noodles. This is my favorite comfort food, especially when I'm sick and need a warm soup that can also help to clear my sinuses. And the best part is that they give very hearty portions so I usually have enough left to save for a second meal.

I say their soup is the way to go. It just tastes SO good. I've had several variations and my usuals will either be the 3 Treasures, wonton (you can never go wrong with wonton noodle soup), or the chicken with mixed vegetables. Sometimes I get the fried fish balls and add them to my soup. Not sure if that's looked down upon, but I love fried fish balls and I think it tastes good together. Their dry hand-drawn noodles still taste good, but the overall dishes are nothing to rave about. I really expected more after having the soup.

The one thing I don't like from here is the fried egg add-on. I tried adding it to my soup once because who doesn't love egg in their soup? But it was way too overdone. 

In terms of spiciness, I will say, if you aren't accustomed to eating spicy food all the time, then going Mild is more than enough for you. Mild heat is usually what I get when I'm sick because I don't want to push my stomach too much. Even with the mild, my lips start to feel the burn halfway into my meal. I find it bearable, but I've known it to be rough on others who don't eat spicy food often. So do what you will with that information.
